paragraphs:
(Achi is one of Benjamin’s ten sons, Genesis 46:21.)
The Achai mentioned in Berakhot 14a was Rabbi Chiyya’s reciter of baraitot. He recited them before Rabbi Chiyya and asked him a question.

notes.text: The biblical parenthesis and the rabbinic notice appear juxtaposed under the same name. This is a source-boundary problem, not evidence that the biblical figure lived in Rabbi Chiyya’s time.

The saved whole Davidson Berakhot14a paragraph explicitly has Achai, the reciter of Rabbi Chiyya’s school, asking Rabbi Chiyya. This supports the reciter role and question direction. The Benjamin-son parenthesis remains juxtaposed in the supplied source and is not an assertion that one person spans the biblical and rabbinic periods. The source-boundary/layout question remains held; no print inspection or broader biblical survey is claimed.

Hyman’s print (vol. I, p. 136) places the biblical parenthesis immediately after the heading אחי and then gives the rabbinic notice. Genesis 46:21 lists Achi among Benjamin’s sons. In Berakhot 14a, Achai of Rabbi Chiyya’s school asks Rabbi Chiyya about interrupting the reading of Hallel or the Megillah. The two passages concern namesakes.
